ca-keo-kho-rau-ram-mien-tay.name: Mekong-style braised goby with Vietnamese coriander
aliases: Peppery braised goby with Vietnamese coriander
ca-keo-kho-rau-ram-mien-tay.serving_basis: One small clay pot of braised fish for four people, served with steamed rice and boiled vegetables.
ca-keo-kho-rau-ram-mien-tay.description: Braised goby with Vietnamese coriander is a familiar Southern Vietnamese family meal. Small goby are gently simmered with fish sauce, pepper and layers of rau ram so the herb infuses the fish. Bếp Việt standardizes the amounts for four servings and uses coconut caramel for a glossy brown finish in a clay or heavy-bottomed pot.
ca-keo-kho-rau-ram-mien-tay.finished_dish: Whole goby are tender and coated in a glossy brown braising sauce; rau ram is fragrant, with a warm finish of pepper and chili.
ca-keo-kho-rau-ram-mien-tay.serving: Serve hot in the clay pot with steamed rice. Add cucumber or boiled vegetables to balance the savory-sweet sauce.
tips: Choose fresh fish and ask the fishmonger to clean it; rinse briefly, then drain well before seasoning.
Marinate for about 15 minutes and layer rau ram between the fish; gently shake the pot instead of stirring so the fish stays intact.
Fish sauce saltiness varies. Taste the sauce before reducing it, and add hot water if the pot dries too quickly.
ca-keo-kho-rau-ram-mien-tay.image_alt: Mekong-style clay pot of whole goby braised with Vietnamese coriander, glossy brown sauce, pepper and chili; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
ca-keo-kho-rau-ram-mien-tay.time_note: About 50 minutes, including preparation, marinating and gentle braising.

ingredients.name: Cleaned goby
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh fish, ask the fishmonger to clean it, then drain before seasoning.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese coriander (rau ram)
ingredients.notes: Pick the leaves, wash and drain; divide into two portions.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Divide between the marinade and braising sauce.

ingredients.name: Coconut caramel
ingredients.notes: Use enough for an amber-brown color; coconut-sugar caramel may be substituted.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the saltiness of the fish sauce.

ingredients.name: Hot water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually for braising; the fish does not need to be submerged.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Season the fish and add a little more at the end.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Bruise it or leave it whole, depending on heat preference.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use only a small pinch when rinsing the fish if needed.

preparation_steps: Briefly rinse the cleaned goby under fresh water and drain. Pick and wash the rau ram; reserve a few tender sprigs for serving.
Mix the fish with fish sauce, coconut caramel, sugar, pepper and chili. Marinate for 15 minutes in the pot you will use, layering rau ram between the fish.
cooking_steps: Set the pot over medium heat until the marinade begins to simmer. Pour hot water down the side of the pot, cover loosely and lower the heat.
Braise gently for 20–25 minutes until the fish is cooked and the sauce lightly thickened. Shake the pot gently once or twice; do not stir vigorously.
Taste and simmer uncovered for a few minutes if you want a thicker sauce. Finish with pepper and the remaining rau ram, then serve hot.

canh-bau-tom-kho-nam-bo.name: Southern Vietnamese bottle-gourd soup with dried shrimp
aliases: Mekong-style gourd and dried shrimp soup
Bottle gourd and dried shrimp soup with scallions
canh-bau-tom-kho-nam-bo.serving_basis: Four bowls of light soup, served hot with a family meal.
canh-bau-tom-kho-nam-bo.description: Bottle-gourd soup with dried shrimp is a gently sweet soup often served with Southern Vietnamese home meals. The dried shrimp are soaked and simmered first to build a naturally savory broth; the gourd is added near the end so it stays green and just tender. This Bếp Việt version uses thin slices for easy preparation and everyday cooking.
canh-bau-tom-kho-nam-bo.finished_dish: A clear, lightly sweet broth with tender pale-green gourd slices, softened dried shrimp, scallions and cilantro.
canh-bau-tom-kho-nam-bo.serving: Ladle the hot soup into a bowl and finish with scallions and cilantro. Serve with steamed rice and a braised or roasted dish.
tips: Soak the dried shrimp in warm water for 10 minutes and rinse to remove surface grit and excess salt; strain and reserve the soaking water if you want a stronger broth.
Add the gourd only after the broth is boiling and cook until just tender; overcooking makes it mushy and clouds the soup.
Taste before adding fish sauce because dried shrimp can already be salty.
canh-bau-tom-kho-nam-bo.image_alt: A bowl of Southern Vietnamese bottle-gourd soup with dried shrimp, pale-green gourd slices in clear broth, scallions and cilantro; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
canh-bau-tom-kho-nam-bo.time_note: About 40 minutes, including soaking the shrimp and simmering the broth.

ingredients.name: Young bottle gourd
ingredients.notes: Peel if the skin is mature; remove spongy seeds from larger gourds, then slice.

ingredients.name: Dried shrimp
ingredients.notes: Rinse, soak in warm water for 10 minutes and rinse again; strain and reserve the soaking water.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Use to simmer the shrimp and cook the soup.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince; briefly sauté if desired.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Optional; omit for a lighter broth.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add gradually after simmering the shrimp.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the saltiness of the dried shrimp.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Optional, in a small amount to balance the broth.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely chop.

preparation_steps: Rinse the dried shrimp and soak them in warm water for 10 minutes until softened. Rinse once more and strain the soaking water if you plan to use it.
Peel and wash the gourd, then slice it thinly. Slice the scallions and cilantro, and mince the shallot.
cooking_steps: Warm the oil in a pot and lightly sauté the shallot. Add the water and dried shrimp, adding some strained soaking water if desired. Bring to a boil, then simmer for about 15 minutes.
Season with salt and a little fish sauce. Once the broth returns to a boil, add the gourd and cook for 2–4 minutes, until tender and slightly translucent.
Taste, turn off the heat before the gourd softens too much, then add scallions and cilantro and ladle into a bowl.

tep-dong-rang-la-chanh.name: Pan-roasted freshwater shrimp with lime leaf
aliases: Tiny freshwater shrimp stir-fried with lime leaves
Pan-roasted small freshwater shrimp with lime leaves
Tiny shrimp roasted with pork fat
tep-dong-rang-la-chanh.serving_basis: One small plate of crisp shrimp to serve with steamed rice and boiled vegetables.
tep-dong-rang-la-chanh.description: Tép đồng rang lá chanh is a rustic dish of tiny freshwater shrimp dry-roasted first, then finished with rendered pork fat, shallot and lime leaf. The Bếp Việt family version uses a restrained sweet-salty seasoning and keeps the two-stage roasting method so the shrimp dry before they are seasoned.
tep-dong-rang-la-chanh.finished_dish: Tiny freshwater shrimp are golden-red, dry-roasted and lightly glossy, with a fragrant scattering of finely shredded lime leaf.
tep-dong-rang-la-chanh.serving: Serve hot as a small side dish with steamed rice, boiled greens or vegetable soup. Add a little lime juice if you prefer a brighter finish.
tips: Choose fresh shrimp, rinse well and drain completely; remaining water makes the shrimp take longer to dry.
Dry-roast over medium-high heat until the shrimp turn pink and dry, then add the fat and seasoning so they remain crisp rather than tough.
Slice the lime leaf very finely and add it at the end to preserve its aroma.
tep-dong-rang-la-chanh.image_alt: A ceramic plate of golden-red pan-roasted tiny freshwater shrimp with finely shredded lime leaf; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
tep-dong-rang-la-chanh.time_note: About 35 minutes, including cleaning, dry-roasting and seasoning the shrimp.

ingredients.name: Tiny freshwater shrimp
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh shrimp, remove debris, rinse and drain thoroughly.

ingredients.name: Pork fat
ingredients.notes: Cut into small cubes and render in the pan.

ingredients.name: Pork cracklings
ingredients.notes: Optional; remove when golden and crisp.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and thinly slice.

ingredients.name: Lime leaves
ingredients.notes: Wash, dry and cut into fine strips.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season after the shrimp have been dry-roasted.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the savory seasoning; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use very little, only if needed.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Coarsely ground.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Optional; add at the end for a brighter flavor.

preparation_steps: Pick through the shrimp, rinse in lightly salted water, rinse again and drain thoroughly. Do not marinate with fish sauce before roasting.
Dice the pork fat, slice the shallots and finely shred the lime leaves. Mix the fish sauce and sugar with a tablespoon of water.
cooking_steps: Heat a pan and add the shrimp without seasoning. Stir over medium-high heat until the moisture evaporates and the shrimp turn pink-red.
Move the shrimp to one side. Render the pork fat in the same pan until golden; add shallots and stir until fragrant, then mix everything together.
Pour in the fish-sauce mixture, lower the heat and stir until it lightly coats the shrimp. Add the cracklings and pepper, then taste.
Turn off the heat and fold in the lime leaf and a few drops of lime juice if desired. Serve hot.

ca-tim-nuong-mo-hanh-mien-tay.name: Southern Vietnamese grilled eggplant with scallion oil
aliases: Grilled eggplant with scallion oil and fish sauce
ca-tim-nuong-mo-hanh-mien-tay.serving_basis: One plate of split grilled eggplant to serve as a vegetable side for four.
ca-tim-nuong-mo-hanh-mien-tay.description: Grilled eggplant with scallion oil is a familiar Southern Vietnamese vegetable side. The eggplant is grilled until tender, its charred skin is peeled back, then it is dressed with scallion oil and garlic-chili fish sauce. This Bếp Việt home version keeps the simple presentation and offers roasted peanuts as an optional finish.
ca-tim-nuong-mo-hanh-mien-tay.finished_dish: Tender grilled eggplant with a few charred purple edges, topped with scallion oil, garlic-chili fish sauce and a little crushed roasted peanut.
ca-tim-nuong-mo-hanh-mien-tay.serving: Split the eggplant lengthwise and serve whole or cut into pieces. Eat warm with steamed rice as a vegetable side.
tips: Choose firm, glossy eggplant of moderate size so the flesh softens before the skin becomes too charred.
For an oven version, preheat to 220°C and turn the eggplant once; test with a skewer to ensure the flesh is fully tender.
Pour hot oil over the scallions so they soften but stay green; season the fish sauce lightly because the eggplant absorbs it quickly.
ca-tim-nuong-mo-hanh-mien-tay.image_alt: A plate of Southern Vietnamese grilled eggplant topped with scallion oil, garlic-chili fish sauce and crushed peanuts; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
ca-tim-nuong-mo-hanh-mien-tay.time_note: About 30 minutes, including preparing the eggplant, grilling and making scallion oil.

ingredients.name: Long purple eggplant
ingredients.notes: Choose 2–3 medium eggplants; wash and keep the stems attached.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash, drain and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Heat and pour over the scallions for the topping.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Mix into the dipping dressing; adjust for saltiness.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Dissolve with the fish sauce and water.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the dipping dressing.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Chili
ingredients.notes: Mince; remove the seeds for less heat.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Optional; crush and sprinkle before serving.

preparation_steps: Wash the eggplant and pat it dry. Prick a few shallow holes in the skin with a toothpick or knife tip so steam can escape while grilling.
Slice the scallions and mince the garlic and chili. Stir the fish sauce, sugar and water together until the sugar dissolves, then add the garlic and chili.
cooking_steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C or prepare a charcoal grill. Grill the eggplants for 15–20 minutes, turning once, until the skins are blistered and the flesh is fully tender.
Heat the oil until hot and pour it over the scallions. Let the eggplant cool slightly, then peel away the larger charred pieces of skin.
Split the eggplant lengthwise and gently spread the flesh on a plate. Add scallion oil and garlic-chili fish sauce, finish with peanuts if desired, and serve warm.

kho-quet-tom-kho-top-mo-nam-bo.name: Southern Vietnamese kho quẹt with dried shrimp and pork cracklings
aliases: Mekong-style caramelized dipping sauce with shrimp
Kho quet with pork and shrimp
Mekong-style kho quet with dried shrimp and pork cracklings
kho-quet-tom-kho-top-mo-nam-bo.serving_basis: One small pot of kho quẹt with a plate of boiled vegetables for four people to share with rice.
kho-quet-tom-kho-top-mo-nam-bo.description: Kho quẹt with dried shrimp and pork cracklings is a savory dipping sauce associated with everyday Southern Vietnamese meals. Dried shrimp, fish sauce and pepper are gently simmered until lightly thickened, then the crisp pork is added for richness. Bếp Việt balances the salty-sweet sauce for a family serving and pairs it with boiled vegetables.
kho-quet-tom-kho-top-mo-nam-bo.finished_dish: A small clay pot of amber-brown, lightly thickened kho quẹt with dried shrimp, pork cracklings, pepper and chili, served beside boiled green beans, carrots and okra.
kho-quet-tom-kho-top-mo-nam-bo.serving: Set the small pot in the middle of the table and dip the boiled vegetables a little at a time. Serve with steamed rice or crisp rice cakes if desired.
tips: Soak the dried shrimp for 5–10 minutes, then taste one before seasoning because salt levels vary.
Render the pork over medium heat until crisp but not burnt; drain most of the fat and keep only about one tablespoon to sauté the aromatics.
Once the fish-sauce mixture begins to thicken, lower the heat and turn it off slightly early because the sauce will continue to thicken as it cools.
search_terms: dried shrimp and pork crackling dip
kho-quet-tom-kho-top-mo-nam-bo.image_alt: A rustic clay pot of glossy Southern Vietnamese kho quẹt with dried shrimp and pork cracklings, served with boiled vegetables; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
kho-quet-tom-kho-top-mo-nam-bo.time_note: About 45 minutes, including soaking the shrimp, rendering pork, simmering the sauce and boiling vegetables.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Cut into small dice to render into pork cracklings.

ingredients.name: Dried shrimp
ingredients.notes: Soak in warm water for 5–10 minutes and drain.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a fragrant variety and add gradually; reduce if very salty.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Mix with the fish sauce so the sauce simmers evenly.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance the savory sauce; start with less if preferred.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Coarsely grind; reserve a little for serving.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Leave whole or slice, depending on heat preference.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Green beans
ingredients.notes: Trim and cut into pieces for dipping.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into batons.

ingredients.name: Okra
ingredients.notes: Wash and trim the stems; leave small pods whole.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the vegetable cooking water.

preparation_steps: Soak the dried shrimp in warm water for 5–10 minutes, rinse and drain. Dice the pork belly, and mince the shallots and garlic.
Wash the green beans, carrot and okra and cut them into dipping-size pieces. Stir the fish sauce, water and sugar together until combined.
cooking_steps: Put the pork belly in a cool pan and render it over medium heat until the fat is released and the cracklings turn golden and crisp. Remove the cracklings and drain most of the fat, leaving about 15 ml.
Sauté the shallots and garlic in the remaining fat until fragrant. Add the dried shrimp and stir until firm and aromatic.

Pour in the fish-sauce mixture and add the pepper and chili. Bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat for 8–12 minutes until lightly thickened. Return the cracklings, taste, turn off the heat and add scallions.
Bring a pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook the green beans, carrot and okra just until tender, drain and serve with the warm kho quẹt.
